source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential cluster spans Colorado (Aurora, Centennial, Denver, Englewood), Utah (Lindon, Salt Lake City, West Jordan), and Nevada (Las Vegas, North Las Vegas), the historic Western United States footprint of ViaWest. According to Flexential own company history page, ViaWest was founded in 1999 and built a strong regional presence across the Western US. In 2017 Peak 10 purchased ViaWest, merging the two regionally dominant data center providers, and the combined company rebranded as Flexential in 2018. Flexential operates 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets as of its current company page, backed by a 2.1 billion dollar inaugural securitization completed in 2021, one of the largest data center green bond asset backed security issuances at the time. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Flexential Salt Lake City – Downtown publishes 2.65 MW of IT capacity across 44,550 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, that load supports roughly 265 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a density associated with GPU training clusters, the same power budget shrinks to about 66 racks. Those figures are assumptions for orientation, not operator claims. The campus does not publish a total power figure, a redundancy tier, or a cooling specification, so no further scaling math is possible from the available data.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for a specific class of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 satisfy audit requirements for financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it to host payment-card data environments. ITAR qualifies it to handle defense-related technical data subject to US export controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare data under HIPAA-aligned frameworks. NIST 800-53 qualifies it for federal or federally adjacent security programs. SSAE 18 is the attestation standard under which the SOC reports are issued, not a separate control framework.

Within Utah, this site ranks sixth among the eight facilities for which this site has read a published MW figure, out of 21 mapped facilities in the state total. Those eight facilities together publish 51.69 MW, and this campus accounts for roughly 5.1 percent of that subtotal. That subtotal excludes the majority of mapped Utah facilities, which publish no capacity figure, so the state's true installed base is larger by an unknown amount. At 2.65 MW, this campus is a mid-tier colocation facility oriented toward compliance-sensitive enterprise workloads rather than large-scale AI training, where power requirements typically run an order of magnitude higher.
